title: The False name in the book
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：false　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 false 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the operator wrote of ① a false name in the book in the log, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② so false that nobody in the station would go near it. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the operator, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the false ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the false name in the book that anybody there had ever seen, or so the log for June 1967 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too false to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the trainee who had come to help; the false ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a false friend at the door, and said that no trainee in his right mind would call it ⑥ as false as the friend at the door they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was false or not, and he said so.

By 1980 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was ⑦ something false, and nothing besides. The trainee from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite false; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the log kept the names of the false ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1983, in the rain, she wrote of another false name in the book in the same log, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ no less false than anybody had expected. ⑩ The false friend at the door that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1985, was the one she could never quite name; the false ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 假（前置定语 a false name in the book：1973 年操作员在运行日志里记下的那件假的名）
B. adj. 假／虚伪（两处加强说法：so false that … 与 no less false than …）
C. adj. 假／虚伪（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 假（表语 too false to do：母亲觉得它太假，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 虚伪（前置定语 a false friend at the door：叔叔把整件事称作一桩虚伪的朋友）
F. adj. 虚伪（同级比较 as false as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩门口那位虚伪的朋友相比）
G. adj. 虚伪（后置定语 something false：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 虚伪（受程度副词修饰 quite false：那位实习生的评价）

items.q: a false name in the book
the false name in the book that
a false friend at the door
The false friend at the door that

answers.why: false 意为“假”，1973 年操作员在运行日志里记下的是“一件假的名”，此处作前置定语 a false name in the book。
false 意为“假”，此处用 so false that 结构，说它假到机房里没人敢靠近。
false 意为“假”，运行日志上 六月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的假书上的假名，等于最高级的说法。
false 意为“假”，母亲认为这件东西“太假了，谁也用不上”，too false to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
false 意为“虚伪”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩虚伪的朋友”，此处作前置定语 a false friend at the door。
false 意为“虚伪”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩门口那位虚伪的朋友一样虚伪”，同级比较用 as false as。
false 意为“虚伪”，运行日志上那半行字要的是“虚伪的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something false。
false 意为“虚伪”，邻机房来的那位实习生认为这套计划“相当虚伪”，quite 修饰原级 false。
false 意为“虚伪”，no less false than 表示“其虚伪不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之虚伪不亚于任何人的预料。
false 意为“虚伪”，母亲 1985 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的虚伪朋友”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1973 年，操作员在运行日志里记下了一件假的名。（a false name in the book）
它假到机房里没有一个人敢靠近。（so false that …）
母亲觉得它太假，谁也用不上。（too false to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩虚伪的朋友。（a false friend at the door）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩门口那位虚伪的朋友一样虚伪。（as false as …）
到了 1980 年，运行日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件虚伪的东西。（something false）
answers: In 1973 the operator wrote of a false name in the book in the log.
It was so false that nobody in the station would go near it.
My mother thought it too false to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a false friend at the door.
He said nobody would call it as false as the friend at the door they had once had.
By 1980 the log asked for nothing but something false.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 false 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1973 the operator wrote of a false name in the book in the log, and nobody forgot it.
It was the false name in the book that anybody there had ever seen, or so the log says.
My mother thought it too false to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a false friend at the door, and nobody argued with him.
The trainee from the next station called the plan quite false, and everybody laughed.
The false ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
